text:
julian: Heads-up — Customer X (search SaaS) just pushed for much lower tail latency on long-context models. Proposal: RFC for 'latency-aware kernel routing' + configurable KV eviction policy. Need to sync scope, acceptance criteria, and launch gates. TL;DR below.
rhea: Important: keep this runtime-only (no API change). Customer wants an SLA target: p99 < 350ms for 2k-token seq on dedicated nodes.
kai: If runtime-only, we need to validate kernel variants (quantized vs fp16) and attention tiling modes. Perf matrix required: p50/p99, mem, tokens/sec, and backpressure behavior. Also define rollback path.
anais: Edge case: streaming + function-calls. If KV eviction happens mid-stream we can end up dropping context needed to finish tool calls. Acceptance criteria must explicitly forbid truncated function-call outputs.
mike: Ops/observability ask: add an eval harness with customer prompts + golden outputs for regression. Canary should start at 1% traffic with automatic circuit-breaker. Also add token-level lat/ cost breakdown dashboards.
julian: Draft acceptance criteria for review: 
  1) p99 latency <= 350ms for 2k tokens on sku-dedicated-1 under steady load (specified QPS).
  2) No more than 0.5% of responses on eval set show content regression vs golden outputs (semantic diff checks).
  3) No incomplete function-call outputs in streaming mode across 100k sampled streams.
  4) Rollback must be achievable within 5 minutes if error-rate >2x baseline or p99 regresses >20%.
  5) Observability: token-level breakdown, KV hit/miss counters, and per-kernel p99 dashboards must be live during canary.
kai: We should also validate the fallback quality delta. Example routing snippet to test in perf harness:
```json
{
  "policy": "latency-first",
  "max_batch_ms": 8,
  "fallback": "cheap-kernel",
  "kv_eviction": { "strategy": "age-based", "min_keep_tokens": 512 }
}
```
rhea: Cost note: reducing batch windows to meet p99 will likely increase GPU utilization and unit cost. CS says Customer X will accept up to ~20% cost uplift if SLA met. Put a cost estimate in RFC.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: RFC placeholder created at /rfc/1765432199-latency-aware-routing.md — please add perf results as comments.
julian: Plan of action: 1) finalize RFC by Fri; 2) eng-ml to produce perf matrix + eval runs; 3) eng-runtime to build canary and routing toggles; 4) launch canary at 1% with circuit-breaker and runbooks; 5) if gates pass (95% of checks), escalate to staged rollout. Owners: julian (PM), kai (eng-runtime), anais (eng-ml), mike (eng-sre).
kai: I'll add simulated KV contention workloads and a harness for per-kernel latency distributions. ETA Wed EOD.
rhea: I'll pull customer test corpus and confirm cost comfort.
mike: I'll draft the rollout runbook (canary commands, rollback commands, dashboards to check).
julian: Great — moving to async review. @channel please call out any missing edge cases (especially around streaming/function-calls and multi-model routing) or additional acceptance criteria. :thumbsup:
